question.text: In 'Lotus Capital AIF' with INR 200 crore total commitments, a 25% drawdown (INR 50 crore) is issued. LP Mr. Sharma (INR 40 crore commitment) DEFAULTS and is fully expelled per the PPM's forfeiture clause. The remaining LPs (INR 160 crore combined) are called to TOP-UP the defaulted amount pro-rata. How much ADDITIONAL will Ms. Priya Shah (INR 20 crore commitment) need to wire beyond her original drawdown?

explanation.text: The Logic: Defaulted amount = 25% x INR 40 crore = INR 10 crore. Non-defaulters (INR 160 crore) split this pro-rata. Ms. Shah's share = 20/160 x INR 10 crore = INR 1.25 crore additional top-up. Her original draw was 25% x INR 20 crore = INR 5 crore; total wired becomes INR 6.25 crore. The Trap: INR 1.00 cr uses wrong denominator. INR 2.50 cr doubles. INR 5.00 cr is her original draw, not the top-up. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers forfeiture math. XXI-B has no parallel (PMS doesn't pool). Manager's Pro-Tip: Always draft a PPM waterfall clause that allows non-defaulting LPs to either top-up (preferred) or new investors to backfill the defaulter's interest - otherwise the fund is short capital mid-deployment.
